date.as_written: subha samvat 1053 sāl phāguna kṛṣṇa 14 roja bṛhaspatīvāra

purpose: merit transfer: by commissioning (coyāgu) this book may the world be delivered from saṃsāra and all beings attain liberation through the Triratna
notes: The colophon names no scribe, patron or owner. 'coyāgu' (Newari, 'had it written') shows the copy was commissioned, but the commissioner is not named. Jinaśrīrāja and Jayaśrī are characters in the text's frame dialogue, not people connected with this copy. The Sanskrit scribal verses are corrupt versions of standard formulas: 'yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā…' and 'bhagnapṛṣṭhakaṭigrīvā… kaṣṭena likhitaṃ śāstraṃ putravat paripālayet'. The era is not named, but 'samvat 1053' agrees with the catalogue's NS 1053; the 'sāl … roja' wording is common in late Newari colophons. Phālguna kṛṣṇa 14 of NS 1053 falls around Feb/Mar 1933 CE. The weekday (Thursday) has not been checked.
